chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Yahya al-Azraq from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'If a man runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah for three or four circuits, then urinates, does he complete his running without ablution?' He said: 'There is no harm, but if he completed his ritual with ablution, it is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.أَشْوَاط: Circuits or rounds of the Sa'i
key_terms.السَّعْي: The ritual running between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwah, the second hill in Mecca

ai.seo_question: Does urination invalidate the Sa'i ritual in Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor impurity (hadath asghar) from urination does not break the validity of Sa'i, reflecting the Shia juristic view that wudu is not a strict condition for the ritual itself. However, he expresses a preference (karahat or istihbab) for maintaining ritual purity throughout the act, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on reverence during worship. This ruling distinguishes between the validity (sahha) and the perfection (kamal) of the rite.
